newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse may start derivatives trade Q2 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse may start derivatives trade Q2 1997.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse will activate a provisional derivatives trading system in the second quarter of 1997 and launch state-of-the-art computer trade in such instruments in 1998, the bourse's president said.

Wieslaw Rozlucki told a seminar on derivatives in the western Polish city of Poznan on Friday that the bourse was likely to begin with derivatives on the WIG-20 share index, interst rates and the dollar/zloty and mark/zloty rates.
He said the bourse would likely start rather with trading futures than options.
"The bourse will have a full, state-of-the-art derivatives system installed in 1998 but a provisional one will be ready in the second quarter of 1997," Rozlucki said.
"There is low demand for derivative instruments in Poland at the moment though interest in them is high. However, we should start preparing for higher demand now," he said.
Rozlucki said that for the development of the derivatives market Poland needed regulations on short-selling, securities lending and margin buying.
He also said taxation on the instruments would be a setback for the fledgling market.
"Taxes for individual investors on derivative transactions, would shackle the development of the market," he said.
Rozlucki also said investors would need a clearing house for derivatives transactions and suggested the Warsaw Stock Exchange could provide start-up capital.
"We would need a clearing house to be ready by the end of the year. The bourse can participate with capital," he said.
